blocks.issue: "...the request is still allowed, provided no explicit deny or other limit (an SCP or permissions boundary) applies." The IAM boundaries page says: "Within the same account, resource-based policies that grant permissions to an IAM user ARN ... are not limited by an implicit deny in an identity-based policy or permissions boundary." (Role ARN grants ARE limited by a boundary; role-session ARN grants are not.) So the blanket "permissions boundary limits the same-account resource-policy allow" is incorrect for IAM users, and the added boundary quote ("maximum permissions that an identity-based policy can grant") does not support it. The SCP part is supported by orgs-scps ("effective permissions are the logical intersection between what is allowed by the SCP ... and what is allowed by the identity-based and resource-based policies"), but that quote is not in the block (the quoted sentence is only "central control over the maximum available permissions"). The explicit-deny part is supported.
blocks.suggestedFix: Inside a single account the rule is looser: if either the identity-based policy or the resource-based policy allows the request and the other does not, the request is still allowed, provided no explicit deny applies. An SCP still limits member-account principals. Drop the permissions boundary from this sentence (or state it exactly: a resource-based policy that names an IAM user ARN is not limited by that user's permissions boundary, but one that names a role ARN is) and replace the boundary quote with iam-boundaries|Within the same account, resource-based policies that grant permissions to an IAM user ARN (that is not an AWS STS federated user principal session) are not limited by an implicit deny in an identity-based policy or permissions boundary.
